papers.title: When Reasoning Helps Action: Monitoring and Steering Chain-of-Thought in Vision-Language-Action Policies
read_sections: III value training and gated token steering
Appendices A/B labeling and value model
papers.finding: The paper separates reasoning correctness from intended behavioral effects. A learned prefix value steers a frozen policy; its substitution study includes corrected reasoning, semantic inversions, gibberish and no reasoning. This is prior art for reasoning-action intervention diagnostics, not evidence that our policy has the same failure. Its judge labels, domain and model differ.

papers.title: SceneReVis
read_sections: A.2 opening and initial optimization steps
papers.finding: The method already combines diagnostic reasoning, atomic scene edits, visual feedback and sequence SFT followed by multi-turn RL. Reverse construction supplies synthetic forward trajectories. Presence-based terms and before/after assessment do not directly establish preservation of every requested instance. Our explicit identity accounting is an evaluation choice, not by itself a new learning method.

papers.finding: The appendix distinguishes numeric geometric tools from language-model judgments, including activity support and sightline obstruction. The listed signatures and docstrings are interface descriptions, not an inspected executable implementation. Multi-mode rules already include retained work access and transition requirements; generic preservation across activities is not a new claim.
